comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces significant competition for talent and limited hiring in 2024, with headcount actions expected to decrease the core workforce by approximately 15% by early 2025. Undesired turnover rates were 5.9% in 2024 and 5.6% in 2023.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and INTC both disclose voluntary attrition/turnover rates for fiscal year 2024, but the rates and definitions differ significantly. AVGO reported a voluntary attrition rate of 2.9% (excluding VMware employees) and 6.2% (including them), describing these as below the industry benchmark. In contrast, INTC reported an 'undesired turnover' rate of 5.9% in 2024 (up from 5.6% in 2023). INTC explicitly excludes voluntary separation packages from this metric, whereas AVGO's metric appears to capture general voluntary attrition without such specific exclusions mentioned in the summary, and AVGO's rates (2.9%-6.2%) encompass a range that overlaps with INTC's 5.9% but is generally lower when excluding merger-related employees.

sentences.text: Our global voluntary attrition rates in fiscal year 2024 were approximately 2.9% (excluding employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger) and approximately 6.2% (including employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger), which are both below the technology industry benchmark (AON, 2024 Salary Increase and Turnover Study - Second Edition, September 2024).

Our undesired turnover rate [footnote 1: Undesired turnover includes all regular Intel employees who voluntarily left Intel, but does not include Intel contract employees, interns, or employees who separated from Intel due to divestiture, retirement, voluntary separation packages, death, job elimination, or redeployment, or Mobileye and other non-integrated subsidiaries employees.] was 5.9% in 2024 and 5.6% in 2023.

AVGO reported a voluntary attrition rate of 2.9% (excluding VMware employees) and 6.2% (including them), both below the industry benchmark.
